hints.title: Impartial Game on Trees
hints.text: This two-player game is an impartial game with normal play convention, analyzable via Sprague-Grundy theorem.

hints.title: Colon Principle on Branching
hints.text: By the colon principle for tree games, appending a branch to a root shifts the subtree Grundy value by one.

hints.title: Six-Periodicity Pattern
hints.text: Computing Grundy values for small tree heights reveals that Grundy value equals zero if and only if n modulo six equals one.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: n: order of the Fibonacci tree
complexity.notes: Periodicity of Sprague-Grundy recurrence reduces game analysis to a constant time check.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating full exponential subtree removals exhausts memory for large n.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Game-theoretic algebraic recurrence yields instant decision.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should demonstrate game theory familiarity and identify periodicity in the recurrence.

solutions.approach: Constant time arithmetic modulo in JavaScript
